verdicts.note: RETIRED version of the ASRM ethics opinion. Superseded record — flag for dedup against W4205755962.
Method for estimating fecundability. A.14's.
Ageing and infertility overview.
No abstract. US infertility service use 1995 vs 2002 — the utilisation trend spanning the mandate era.
Male and female age factors in fertility.

**SR and meta-analysis of ART COMPLIANCE (dropout) RATES.** Third record on discontinuation. Between access and births sits a leak that this quantifies: couples who start treatment and stop. Arm 2's mandate effects have to pass through it.
No abstract. Economic impact of ART.
1967 public health and population change.
Happiness and selection into parenthood.
Help-seeking for subfecundity across FIVE EUROPEAN COUNTRIES — cross-national variation in the entry step, under different access regimes.
RNA modifications in ageing.
No abstract. Who receives a medical evaluation for infertility in the US.
Agenda-setting piece on integrating fertility and infertility research. Useful framing for the chapter's boundary with Wall 4.
Retrospective time-to-pregnancy sampling bias. A measurement warning for the fecundity literature P4 borrows from.
No abstract. INEQUITY BETWEEN MALE AND FEMALE COVERAGE in state infertility laws. Mandate content varies on a dimension arm 2's binary treatment ignores entirely.
CDC ART Surveillance 2011.
Review of racial disparities in fertility care.

**Long-term parenthood outcomes DURING IVF and AFTER DISCONTINUATION of unsuccessful IVF.** Fourth record measuring what happens to couples the treatment did not deliver for — the counterfactual arm 1 sets to zero.
Social cues and discretionary utilisation of infertility care. A non-price determinant of the same treatment take-up arm 2 attributes to coverage.
Qualitative fertility-education perceptions.
Infertility-specific distress in patients.
Fertility counselling practice chapter.

**'Does the concept work?' — a PROSPECTIVE 2-year follow-up of 519 women through the Fertility Assessment and Counselling Clinic.** With the 6-year and 8-year follow-ups, the Danish FAC programme now supplies P6 with a cohort followed from a belief intervention to realized childbearing at three horizons. This is the closest thing A.17 has to a designed test of the induced-postponement channel.

No abstract. EDUCATIONAL GRADIENTS in the prevalence of MAR births, comparative. Composition again: if MAR births concentrate among the highly educated, the population share and the counterfactual share diverge.
Qualitative: adoption as sequenced AFTER medicalised infertility, not substituted for it. Refines the substitution margin the economics papers estimate.
Review of education and fertility in Europe.

**'LIKELIHOOD OF NATURAL CONCEPTION FOLLOWING TREATMENT BY IVF.'** The counterfactual named in a title. Fifth such record; the upper-bound argument now rests on a small but coherent literature rather than on an assumption.
Public-health assessment of a North American PUBLICLY FUNDED IVF PROGRAM — Quebec's, seen from the evaluation side. Pairs with the NEJM record.
Capri Workshop Group retrospective on IVF, noting its growing demographic role.
Predicting time to menopause.
MAR and preterm birth, Quebec cohort.
Australian understanding of age decline and attitudes to ovarian reserve screening.
Paternity leave flexibility and maternal health.
Kazakh women's age-fertility awareness.
Six-year perceptions follow-up of the same Danish FAC cohort.
No abstract. An EMPLOYER's experience with infertility coverage — the self-insured margin the ERISA record says matters most.
Social egg freezing motivations and treatment experience, single centre.
Parenthood penalty in mental health.
Information intervention on delay risks for students.
Qualitative UK fertility decision-making.
Statistical modelling of age at first parenthood and progression. Methods.
Socioeconomic profile of couples using Brazil's public system. Wall 8 — tag SECONDARY_LMIC.

**'How effective is assisted reproduction technology? A MODEL ASSESSMENT'** — Leridon's method applied to effectiveness rather than to compensation. Same author, same modelling family as the 2004 anchor; the two should be appraised together.
Infertility care in under-resourced settings. Wall 8.
Dyadic population-level sociodemographics of US MAR births — includes MEN, which the ART registries usually cannot.
Handbook chapter on desires, intentions and behaviour.
Fertility preferences in multiple sclerosis.
Uncertainty in fertility preferences.
Preservation in haematological malignancy, Japan.

**'Coverage of Infertility Treatment and Fertility Outcomes: DO WOMEN CATCH UP?'** — the preprint of the Machado & Sanz-de-Galdeano anchor, and its subtitle is the chapter's whole question. Catching up is recuperation; whether coverage produces it is arm 2 answering P4's question. Version-of-record duplicate — flag.
Latina vs Caucasian infertility service use.
ART use in peripartum cardiomyopathy patients.
Handbook chapter titled '12 Fertility'.
'The family clock' — lived experience of fertility decisions six years after FAC. Qualitative arm of the Danish cohort.
No abstract. Utilisation determinants WITHIN a comprehensive-mandate state — isolates what still binds once price is removed.
Miscarriage and parental investment. B.5's.
Dissertation on the experience of the ART pathway.

**EXPANDED EMPLOYER FERTILITY BENEFITS at a single centre, 2017-2021.** The employer margin is where US access is actually decided for the self-insured two-thirds — the population state mandates cannot reach. Small setting, exactly the right exposure.
Patients seeking care in a low-income setting. Wall 8.
Fertility treatment and ovarian cancer risk.
